{{for|topological indices in mathematics|Atiyah–Singer index theorem}}
In the fields of [[chemical graph theory]], [[topology (chemistry)|molecular topology]], and [[mathematical chemistry]], a '''topological index''', also known as a '''connectivity index''', is a type of [[molecular descriptor]] that is calculated based on the [[molecular graph]] of a chemical compound.<ref name="isbn3-527-29913-0">{{cite book |author1=Hendrik Timmerman |author2=Todeschini, Roberto |author3=Viviana Consonni |author4=Raimund Mannhold |author5=Hugo Kubinyi | title = Handbook of Molecular Descriptors | publisher = Wiley-VCH | location = Weinheim | year = 2002 | isbn = 3-527-29913-0 }}</ref>  Topological indices are  numerical parameters of a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] which characterize its [[topology]] and are usually [[graph invariant|invariant]] under isomorphism. Topological indices are used for example in the development of [[quantitative structure-activity relationship]]s (QSARs) in which the biological activity or other properties of molecules are [[correlation|correlated]] with their [[chemical structure]].<ref name="isbn0-12-406560-0">{{cite book | author1 = Hall, Lowell H. | author2 = Kier, Lemont B. | title = Molecular connectivity in chemistry and drug research | publisher = Academic Press | location = Boston | year = 1976 | isbn = 0-12-406560-0 | url = https://archive.org/details/molecularconnect00kier }}</ref>

== Calculation ==

Topological descriptors are derived from hydrogen-suppressed molecular graphs, in which the atoms are represented by vertices and the bonds by edges. The connections  between the atoms can be described by various types of topological matrices (e.g., distance or adjacency matrices), which can be mathematically manipulated so as to derive a single number, usually known as graph invariant, graph-theoretical index or topological index.<ref name="pmid17508935">{{cite journal |vauthors=González-Díaz H, Vilar S, Santana L, Uriarte E | title = Medicinal chemistry and bioinformatics--current trends in drugs discovery with networks topological indices | journal = Current Topics in Medicinal Chemistry | volume = 7 | issue = 10 | pages = 1015–29 | year = 2007 | pmid = 17508935 | doi = 10.2174/156802607780906771| url = https://www.eurekaselect.com/article/23378 | archive-url =  | url-status =  | archive-date =  | url-access = subscription }}</ref><ref name="pmid18297652">{{cite journal |vauthors=González-Díaz H, González-Díaz Y, Santana L, Ubeira FM, Uriarte E | title = Proteomics, networks and connectivity indices | journal = Proteomics | volume = 8 | issue = 4 | pages = 750–78 |date=February 2008 | pmid = 18297652 | doi = 10.1002/pmic.200700638 | s2cid = 20599466 }}</ref> As a result, the topological index can be defined as two-dimensional descriptors that can be easily calculated from the molecular graphs, and do not depend on the way the graph is depicted or labeled and no need of energy minimization of the chemical structure.

==Types ==

The simplest topological indices do not recognize double bonds and atom types (C, N, O etc.) and ignore hydrogen atoms ("hydrogen suppressed") and defined for connected undirected [[molecular graph]]s only.<ref name="king">{{cite book | author = King, R. Bruce | title = Chemical applications of topology and graph theory: a collection of papers from a symposium held at the University of Georgia, Athens, Georgia, U. S. A., 18–22 April 1983 | publisher = Elsevier | location = Amsterdam | year = 1983 | isbn = 0-444-42244-7 }}</ref> More sophisticated topological indices also take into account the [[orbital hybridisation|hybridization state]] of each of the atoms contained in the molecule. The [[Hosoya index]] is the first topological index recognized in chemical graph theory, and it is often referred to as "the" topological index.<ref>{{Cite journal | last=Hosoya | first=Haruo | title=Topological index. A newly proposed quantity characterizing the topological nature of structural isomers of saturated hydrocarbons | journal=Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan | volume=44 | issue=9 | year=1971 | pages=2332–2339 | doi=10.1246/bcsj.44.2332 | doi-access=free }}.</ref> Other examples include the [[Wiener index]], [[Randić's molecular connectivity index]], [[Balaban's J index]],<ref name="urlDescriptors: Topological Descriptors">{{cite web | url = http://www.codessa-pro.com/descriptors/topo/index.htm | title = Topological Descriptors |vauthors=Katritzky AR, Karelson M, Petrukhin R | year = 2002 | publisher = University of Florida | access-date = 2009-05-06}}</ref> and the TAU descriptors.<ref name = "Pal_1988">{{Cite journal | title =  A new topochemical descriptor (TAU) in molecular connectivity concept: Part I--Aliphatic compounds |vauthors=Pal DK, Sengupta C, De AU | year = 1988 | journal = Indian J. Chem. | pages = 734–739 | volume = 27B }}</ref><ref name = "Pal_1989">{{Cite journal | title =  Introduction of A Novel Topochemical Index and Exploitation of Group Connectivity Concept to Achieve Predictability in QSAR and RDD |vauthors=Pal DK, Sengupta C, De AU | year = 1989 | journal = Indian J. Chem. | volume = 28B | pages = 261–267 }}</ref>  The extended topochemical atom (ETA)<ref name = "Roy_2003">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Ghosh G | title = Extended Topochemical Atom (ETA) Indices in the Valence Electron Mobile (VEM) Environment as Tools | url = http://www.doaj.org/abstract?id=100373 | journal = Internet Electronic Journal of Molecular Design | volume = 2  | pages =  599–620 | year = 2003 }}</ref> indices have been developed based on refinement of TAU descriptors.

=== Global and local indices ===

[[Hosoya index]] and [[Wiener index]] are '''global (integral) indices''' to describe entire molecule, Bonchev and Polansky introduced '''local (differential) index''' for every atom in a molecule.<ref name="king"/> Another examples of local indices are modifications of Hosoya index.<ref name= tmi >{{Cite journal | title = An optimization of the procedure for the calculation of Hosoya's index | doi = 10.1007/BF01166946 | year = 1991 | author = Trofimov MI | journal = Journal of Mathematical Chemistry | pages = 327–332 | volume = 8 | issue = 1 | s2cid = 121743373 }}</ref>

=== Discrimination capability and superindices ===

A topological index may have the same value for a subset of different molecular graphs, i.e. the index is unable to discriminate the graphs from this subset. The '''discrimination capability''' is very important characteristic of topological index. To increase the discrimination capability a few topological indices may be combined to '''superindex'''.<ref>{{Cite journal | title = Isomer discrimination by topological information approach | doi = 10.1002/jcc.540020202 | year = 1981 | journal = Journal of Computational Chemistry | volume = 2 | issue = 2 |vauthors=Bonchev D, Mekenyan O, Trinajstić N | pages = 127–148 | s2cid = 120705298 }}</ref>

=== Computational complexity ===

[[Computational complexity theory|Computational complexity]] is another important characteristic of topological index. The Wiener index, Randic's molecular connectivity index, Balaban's J index may be calculated by fast algorithms, in contrast to Hosoya index and its modifications for which non-exponential  algorithms are unknown.<ref name="tmi"/>

== Application ==

=== QSAR ===

[[QSAR]]s represent predictive [[statistical model|model]]s derived from application of statistical tools correlating [[biological activity]] (including desirable therapeutic effect and undesirable side effects) of chemicals (drugs/toxicants/environmental pollutants) with descriptors representative of [[molecular geometry|molecular structure]] and/or [[molecular property|properties]]. QSARs are being applied in many disciplines for example [[risk assessment]], toxicity prediction, and regulatory decisions<ref name="Tong_2005">{{cite journal | vauthors =  Tong W, Hong H, Xie Q, Shi L, Fang H, Perkins R | title =  Assessing QSAR Limitations – A Regulatory Perspective | journal =  Current Computer-Aided Drug Design | volume =  1 | issue =  2 | pages =  195–205 | date =  April 2005 | doi =  10.2174/1573409053585663 | url =  http://www.bentham.org/ccadd/contabs/cad1-2.htm#5 | url-status =  dead | archive-url =  https://web.archive.org/web/20100620101649/http://bentham.org/ccadd/contabs/cad1-2.htm#5 | archive-date =  2010-06-20 | url-access =  subscription }}</ref> in addition to [[drug discovery]] and [[drug development|lead optimization]].<ref name="pmid13677480">{{cite journal | author = Dearden JC | title = In silico prediction of drug toxicity | journal = Journal of Computer-aided Molecular Design | volume = 17 | issue = 2–4 | pages = 119–27 | year = 2003 | pmid = 13677480 | doi = 10.1023/A:1025361621494 | bibcode = 2003JCAMD..17..119D | s2cid = 21518449 }}</ref>

For example,  ETA indices have been applied in the development of predictive QSAR/QSPR/QSTR models.<ref name = "ETA_applications">{{cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Ghosh G | title = QSTR with extended topochemical atom indices. 2. Fish toxicity of substituted benzenes | journal = Journal of Chemical Information and Computer Sciences | volume = 44 | issue = 2 | pages = 559–67 | year = 2004 | pmid = 15032536 | doi = 10.1021/ci0342066 }}; {{cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Ghosh G | title = QSTR with extended topochemical atom indices. Part 5: Modeling of the acute toxicity of phenylsulfonyl carboxylates to Vibrio fischeri using genetic function approximation | journal = Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry | volume = 13 | issue = 4 | pages = 1185–94 |date=February 2005 | pmid = 15670927 | doi = 10.1016/j.bmc.2004.11.014 }}; {{cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Ghosh G | title = QSTR with extended topochemical atom (ETA) indices. VI. Acute toxicity of benzene derivatives to tadpoles (Rana japonica) | journal = Journal of Molecular Modeling | volume = 12 | issue = 3 | pages = 306–16 |date=February 2006 | pmid = 16249936 | doi = 10.1007/s00894-005-0033-7 | s2cid = 30293729 }}; {{cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Sanyal I, Roy PP | title = QSPR of the bioconcentration factors of non-ionic organic compounds in fish using extended topochemical atom (ETA) indices | journal = SAR and QSAR in Environmental Research | volume = 17 | issue = 6 | pages = 563–82 |date=December 2006 | pmid = 17162387 | doi = 10.1080/10629360601033499 | bibcode = 2006SQER...17..563R | s2cid = 10707472 }}; {{cite journal |vauthors=Roy K, Ghosh G | title = QSTR with extended topochemical atom (ETA) indices. 9. Comparative QSAR for the toxicity of diverse functional organic compounds to Chlorella vulgaris using chemometric tools | journal = Chemosphere | volume = 70 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–12 |date=November 2007 | pmid = 17765287 | doi = 10.1016/j.chemosphere.2007.07.037 | bibcode =2007Chmsp..70....1R }}</ref>
